title: concurrent-tool-runner: parallel tool invocation + OpenAI function_call compatibility updates
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: customers increasingly chain multiple tool calls per turn and want lower tail latency by running compatible tools in parallel, plus predictable result injection and idempotent retries. This PR introduces a server-side concurrent tool runner, extends the OpenAI-compatible function_call surface to allow explicit parallel calls and tool-result references, and updates SDK helpers and streaming merge semantics to keep the API stable for existing clients. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: add services/inference/tool_runner/concurrent_runner with a pluggable execution strategy (sequential | parallel | hybrid), a run_id-based idempotency layer for retries, and deterministic merge ordering for structured output injection. 2) api/openai-compat: extend function_call payload with optional keys: "parallel_calls" (array of tool names), "tool_result_refs" (map-like list of result identifiers), and "injection_policy" (deterministic | merge_stream | attach_raw). The compat layer translates these into internal execution plans and exposes merged streaming boundaries to callers. 3) streaming: improve chunk merging to reduce interleaving artifacts when multiple tool streams are active; add a small backpressure window to avoid head-of-line blocking in multi-tool flows. 4) SDKs: python & typescript helpers to create and await parallel tool futures, helpers to submit a single composite call that the server will execute in parallel when possible, and a deterministic merge utility for client-side local execution. 5) docs & tests: update openapi spec, add e2e test harness that exercises parallel function calls, and add unit tests covering retry idempotency and injection ordering. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains sequential tool execution; the new keys are opt-in. Also preserved the original function_call semantics for single-tool usage to avoid breaking existing OpenAI-compatible clients. Rationale: moving parallelism into the platform lets us optimize batching and GPU utilization while keeping SDK ergonomics simple; adding run_id/idempotency reduces duplicate side-effects for retried calls. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag concurrent_tool_runner.enabled. Initially enabled in staging and can be opt-in per-tenant via config; will be enabled by default after 2 weeks of telemetry. Related: linked_linear ENG-4123 ENG-4181. Notes: this PR intentionally avoids introducing a new RPC surface; changes are translations within the compat layer and runtime to minimize client churn.

release_notes: Added server-side concurrent tool runner (opt-in). Extended OpenAI-compatible function_call payload to support parallel_calls and tool result references. SDK helpers for parallel tool orchestration (Python & TypeScript). Streaming merge improvements to reduce interleaving when multiple tool streams are active.
